3. A method of making a fertile mouse that is homozygous for a transgenic antibody heavy chain locus, the mouse having a genome that
4. The method of any preceding claim, wherein an ADAM6-encoding nucleotide sequence is inserted on one or both chromosomes 12.
5. The method of any preceding claim, with the alternative that each organism is a rat instead of a mouse and each said chromosome is a chromosome 6 instead of chromosome 12.
6. The method of any preceding claim, wherein mouse ADAM6a and ADAM6b-encoding nucleotide sequences are inserted, such that the final fertile mouse can express both ADAM6a and ADAM6b proteins.
7. A mouse (optionally a male mouse) that is homozygous for a transgenic antibody heavy chain locus, the mouse having a genome that
8. A rat (optionally a male rat) that is homozygous for a transgenic antibody heavy chain locus, the rat having a genome that

9. The mouse or rat of any one of claims 7 or 8, or method according to any one of claims 1-6, wherein an inserted ADAM6-encoding nucleotide sequence is inserted (i) within one or both transgenic heavy chain loci or (ii) within 20 Mb of one or both transgenic heavy chain loci.

10. The method according to any one of claims 1-6, wherein mouse ADAM6a and ADAM6b-encoding nucleotide sequences are inserted, such that the final fertile mouse can express both ADAM6a and ADAM6b, or the mouse or rat of any one of claims 7-9, wherein the genome comprises inserted expressible mouse ADAM6a and ADAM6b-encoding nucleotide sequences.
11. The mouse or rat of any one of claims 7-10, or method according to any one of claims 1-6, 9 or 10, wherein the genome is homozygous for each inserted ADAM6 gene.

12. The mouse or rat of any one of claims 7-11, or method according to any one of claims 1-6, or 9-11, wherein the genome comprises one or more transgenic light chain loci each comprising one or more human light chain V gene segments and one or more light chain J gene segments operably connected upstream of a light chain constant region (eg, an endogenous mouse C kappa constant region).

13. The mouse or rat or method of claim 12, wherein the one or more transgenic light chain loci each comprise only one human light chain V gene segment and only one light chain J gene segment operably connected upstream of a light chain constant region (eg, an endogenous mouse C kappa constant region), optionally wherein there is only one such transgenic light chain locus in the mouse or rat genome.
14. A method of isolating an antibody or nucleotide sequence encoding said antibody, the method comprising

(a) immunising a mouse or rat) according to any one of claim 7-11 with a human target antigen such that the vertebrate produces antibodies; and (b) isolating from the mouse or rat an antibody that specifically binds to said antigen and/or isolating a nucleotide sequence encoding at least the heavy and/or the light chain variable regions of said antibody; and optionally wherein the variable regions of said antibody are subsequently joined to a human constant region.
15. A cell line (eg, an immortalised cell line, ES cell or iPS cell line), B-cell, hybridoma or stem cell derived from a mouse as recited in any one of claims 7 and 9-13.
